notes:
I couldn't write these notes. My research tool stopped working before any pages loaded, so I didn't read a single source on Psalm 103.

Your rules say to report only what the pages say and to leave out anything I couldn't find. With nothing read, there's nothing I can properly include. I've also chosen not to write notes from memory, because that would break the "never fill a gap from your own knowledge" rule and there would be no real URLs to cite.

If you ask again in a new message, these are the pages I'd read first:

- **Verse-by-verse sources:** enduringword.com (Psalm 103 commentary); the Gill, Ellicott and Pulpit Commentary pages for Psalm 103 on biblehub.com; preceptaustin.org's Psalm 103 page; and the netbible.org translator notes.
- **Where traditions differ:** the main one is likely v. 3 ("heals all your diseases") and whether it promises physical healing today. I'd compare what the Pentecostal sites (ag.org, enduringword.com, samstorms.org) say with the Reformed and Baptist ones (desiringgod.org, gty.org, ligonier.org). I'd also check the Wesleyan and Lutheran sites on forgiveness in vv. 10–12.
- **Other views:**
  - Augustine's sermon on this psalm on newadvent.org (in the Greek and Latin Bibles it's numbered Psalm 102).
  - Catholic and Orthodox pages on catholic.com and oca.org.
  - Anything the sites say about prosperity or word-of-faith readings of v. 5 ("satisfies you with good things"), for example on gotquestions.org.
